places.name: Borong
places.summary: A quiet eco-tourism village near Ravangla at 5,800 ft, with river hot springs, village cottages and the trek to Maenam peak.
places.seoTitle: Borong, Sikkim — hot springs and village stays near Ravangla
places.seoDescription: Borong near Ravangla: Borong Tsachu hot springs on the Rangeet, village cottages, birdwatching and the trek to Maenam peak.

overview.text:
Borong is a small village at 5,800 ft in south Sikkim, near Ravangla, that has grown into a base for eco-tourism. Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali families live side by side here, and temples, monasteries and a mosque share the hillside.

The big draw is Borong Tsachu, a set of hot springs on the bank of the Rangeet river that locals say have healing properties. Walkers come for the trails: the long Damthang–Tendong–Ravangla–Maenam–Borong route, or the climb towards Maenam peak for sunrise over the snow mountains. The surrounding forest is good for birds — look for scarlet minivets, black magpies and Himalayan pheasants. Stay in one of the village cottages and slow down.

items.body: Soak in the Borong Tsachu hot springs by the Rangeet.
Trek towards Maenam peak for sunrise over the snow mountains.

best_time.text: Come in February for the riverbank festival, or in August–September for Pang Lhabsol at nearby Ravangla.

where_to_stay.text: Stay in one of the cosy cottages in the village itself — Borong is small, so you are never far from the trails or the hot springs.

places.name: Ganesh Tok
places.summary: A small hilltop Ganesh temple above Gangtok at about 6,500 ft, known for its views over the city to Kanchenjunga.
places.seoTitle: Ganesh Tok, Gangtok — timings and views
places.seoDescription: Ganesh Tok: a hilltop Ganesh temple above Gangtok at about 6,500 ft with views to Kanchenjunga. Open 6 am–7 pm.

images.commons: File:Ganesh Tok in Gangtok district, East Sikkim 01.jpg
images.alt: The small Ganesh Tok temple on its hilltop above Gangtok
images.caption: Ganesh Tok, Gangtok

overview.text:
Ganesh Tok is a small temple to Lord Ganesh on a hilltop above Gangtok, at roughly 6,500 feet. Most people come for the view as much as the shrine: on a clear day the snow peaks of the Himalayas, Kanchenjunga among them, line up across the horizon, and the city spreads out below.

The climb up from the road is short, and prayer flags flutter along the way. Early morning and late afternoon give the clearest light, when the sky over the range turns gold. The temple is open from 6 am to 7 pm. Pair it with Hanuman Tok, another hilltop temple nearby, and the Tashi View Point for a half-day loop of Gangtok's viewpoints.

places.name: Himalayan Zoological Park
places.summary: Gangtok's hillside zoo for Himalayan species — red pandas, snow leopards and black bears — explored on foot or by car.
places.seoTitle: Himalayan Zoological Park, Gangtok — red pandas and snow leopards
places.seoDescription: Himalayan Zoological Park, Gangtok: red pandas, snow leopards and Himalayan black bears in forest enclosures. Open 8 am–3 pm; walk or drive through.

images.commons: File:Gangtok Bulbuley Himalayan Zoological Park Captive Red Panda Lyingdown.jpg
images.alt: A red panda resting on a branch at the Himalayan Zoological Park
images.caption: Red panda, Himalayan Zoological Park

overview.text:
The Himalayan Zoological Park spreads over forested hillside on the edge of Gangtok and is the easiest place in Sikkim to see the animals of the high Himalayas up close. Its enclosures are built to feel like natural habitat, and the stars are the Himalayan black bear, the red panda and the snow leopard.

You can drive through in your own vehicle or walk the trails that wind between the enclosures, which is the better way to spot birds: Himalayan monals, sunbirds, eagles and owls all turn up. Note the short hours: the park opens at 8 am and closes at 3 pm, so go in the morning. It sits close to Tashi View Point and Ganesh Tok, which makes an easy half-day together.

items.title: Getting round
items.body: Drive through or walk the trails

items.title: Animals
items.body: Red panda, snow leopard, Himalayan black bear

places.name: Lingdum (Ranka) Monastery
places.summary: A large Zurmang Kagyu monastery outside Gangtok, with a muralled prayer hall and courtyards; open 6 am–6 pm.
places.seoDescription: Lingdum, or Ranka, Monastery near Gangtok: a Zurmang Kagyu monastery with a muralled prayer hall and mountain views. Open 6 am–6 pm.

images.commons: File:Lingdum Zurmang Kharwang Gonpa or Ranka Monastery, East Sikkim. 05.jpg
images.alt: The main hall of Lingdum Monastery with prayer flags
images.caption: Lingdum (Ranka) Monastery

overview.text:
Lingdum Monastery, also known as Ranka Monastery, lies in the hills outside Gangtok and belongs to the Zurmang Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism. Its grand buildings have made it a backdrop for several Bollywood films, but it is very much a working monastery.

The main prayer hall is the heart of the complex, its walls covered in detailed murals of Buddhist deities. Beyond it lie courtyards, meditation halls and the monks' quarters, with prayer wheels turning in the breeze. Come at prayer time to hear the chanting, and step outside the walls for the view over the valley. It is open from 6 am to 6 pm. Banjhakri Falls is nearby if you want to combine the two.

places.name: Phodong Monastery
places.summary: An early-18th-century Karma Kagyu monastery 28 km north of Gangtok, home to about 260 monks.
places.seoDescription: Phodong Monastery, 28 km from Gangtok on the North Sikkim road: early-18th-century, about 260 monks, old murals. Open 9 am–5 pm.

images.commons: File:Phodong "Karma Thubten Tashi ChoKhorling" Monastery, Phodong, North Sikkim, India 01.jpg
images.caption: Phodong Monastery

overview.text:
Phodong Monastery stands on a hillside 28 km from Gangtok, on the road into North Sikkim. It was built in the early 18th century, on the site of an older monastery, and is one of three that the 9th Karmapa founded in Sikkim, together with Rumtek and Ralang.

About 260 monks live here today, and the main hall holds a fine collection of old murals and statues. The setting is part of the appeal: the monastery looks over the valley towards the snow peaks. Visitors can sit in on prayers, and the monastery comes alive at festivals such as Pang Lhabsol and Losar, when monks perform masked dances. It is open from 9 am to 5 pm — an easy stop on the way to Mangan, Lachen or Lachung.

places.name: Ralang Monastery
places.summary: A large Kagyu monastery 6 km from Ravangla, built in 1995 beside the older Ralang Gompa, known for its thangkas.
places.seoDescription: Ralang Monastery, 6 km from Ravangla: a Kagyu monastery built in 1995 beside the old Ralang Gompa, with paintings, thangkas and Pang Lhabsol in September.

images.alt: The golden roofs of Ralang Monastery
images.caption: Ralang Monastery

overview.text:
Ralang Monastery lies six kilometres from Ravangla in south Sikkim, and belongs to the Kagyu school. The present building, the Palchen Choeling Monastic Institute, was built in 1995 by the 12th Gyaltsab Rinpoche in traditional Tibetan style; the older Ralang Gompa stands just to the west and is worth the short walk.

Inside, the monastery holds an extensive collection of paintings and thangkas. The best time to visit is during Pang Lhabsol, usually in September, when Mount Kangchenjunga is worshipped with masked dances. Combine it with the Buddha Park at Ravangla and the hot springs at Borong.

items.body: See the extensive collection of paintings and thangkas inside the new monastery.
Walk to the older Ralang Gompa, just to the west of the new building.
Time your visit for Pang Lhabsol, usually in September, when Kangchenjunga is worshipped.

places.name: Rinchenpong
places.summary: A quiet hill town in West Sikkim at 5,576 ft, known for Reesum Monastery, walking trails and its 'poisoned lake'.
places.seoDescription: Rinchenpong, West Sikkim (5,576 ft): Reesum Monastery, trekking routes and the legendary 'poisoned lake', 123 km from Gangtok.

images.commons: File:Rinchenpong Monastery, Rinchenpong (Richenpong) and Kaluk , West Sikkim 01.jpg
images.caption: Rinchenpong Monastery

overview.text:
Rinchenpong is a small hill town in West Sikkim, at 5,576 ft near the village of Kaluk. It lies about 123 km west of Gangtok and 47 km south of Gyalshing — far enough off the main circuit to stay quiet.

The town is known for the Reesum Monastery and for the walking trails that run through the surrounding villages and forest. It also has a story: near town is bikh-pokhri, the "poisoned lake", where locals are said to have poisoned the only water source during a battle between the Chogyal's forces and an invading British army. Come for slow days, village walks and wide views, as an easier-going alternative to busier Pelling.

how_to_reach.text: Rinchenpong is about 123 km west of Gangtok and 47 km south of Gyalshing, by road.

places.name: Samdruptse (Guru Padmasambhava statue)
places.summary: The hill opposite Namchi crowned by a 135 ft statue of Guru Padmasambhava, completed in 2004.
places.seoTitle: Samdruptse, Namchi — the Guru Padmasambhava statue
places.seoDescription: Samdruptse hill opposite Namchi: a 135 ft statue of Guru Padmasambhava, Sikkim's patron saint, completed in February 2004.

images.commons: File:Guru Padmasambhava statue in Samdruptse Hill, Namchi, district of South Sikkim 08.jpg
images.alt: The giant statue of Guru Padmasambhava on Samdruptse hill
images.caption: Guru Padmasambhava statue, Samdruptse

overview.text:
Samdruptse is the forested hill facing Namchi, and on its top stands a 135 ft statue of Guru Padmasambhava, the Buddhist teacher revered across Sikkim as Guru Rinpoche. Completed in February 2004, the figure can be seen from far across the valley.

A path leads up through prayer flags to the base of the statue, where pilgrims walk round it and turn the prayer wheels. On a clear day the view stretches to the snow peaks. It is a short drive from Namchi town, and pairs naturally with Siddhesvara Dham on Solophok hill, about 5 km from Namchi on the other side of town.

items.body: Walk up to the base of the 135 ft Guru Padmasambhava statue.
Drive across Namchi to Siddhesvara Dham on Solophok hill, about 5 km from town.

places.name: Sanga Choeling Monastery
places.summary: A 1697 Nyingma monastery on the ridge above Pelling, reached on foot by a steep forest path.
places.seoDescription: Sanga Choeling, built in 1697 on the ridge above Pelling: one of Sikkim's oldest monasteries, with 17th-century clay statues, reached by a 4 km forest walk.

images.alt: Sanga Choeling Monastery on its forested ridge
images.caption: Sanga Choeling Monastery

overview.text:
Sanga Choeling is one of the oldest monasteries in Sikkim, built in 1697 by Lama Lhatsün Chempo on a ridge high above Pelling. Its name means "island of the secret mantra teachings", and it belongs to the Nyingma school.

There is no road to the door: you reach it by a steep 4 km path through forest, which is half the reason to go. The reward is a quiet monastery with clay statues from the 17th century — it has burned and been rebuilt several times — and wide views over the ridges around Pelling. The monastery is reserved for men only. It sits on the West Sikkim pilgrimage circuit with Pemayangtse, the Rabdentse ruins, Khecheopalri Lake, Yuksom and Tashiding.

places.name: Seven Sisters Waterfall
places.summary: A roadside cascade on the North Sikkim highway near Tumlong, where four of seven falls are visible from below.
places.seoTitle: Seven Sisters Waterfall, Sikkim — on the North Sikkim road
places.seoDescription: Seven Sisters Waterfall near Tumlong on the road north of Gangtok: four of its seven cascades visible from below, open 8 am–5 pm.

images.alt: The Seven Sisters Waterfall dropping through forest beside the road
images.caption: Seven Sisters Waterfall

overview.text:
The Seven Sisters Waterfall drops in a series of cascades through forest beside the road north of Gangtok, close to Tumlong — the old royal capital of Sikkim between 1793 and 1861.

From the road you can see four of the seven falls; the other three are higher up the cliff. A small footbridge crosses the stream so you can stand right in the spray. Local legend says seven celestial sisters came down from the heavens to bathe here and never left. The site is open from 8 am to 5 pm. Take care on wet rocks.

items.title: Cascades
items.body: Four of seven visible from below
Cross the footbridge over the stream for a close view of the falls.
Look up for the three upper cascades above the four you see from the road.

places.name: Siddhesvara Dham (Char Dham), Namchi
places.summary: A Hindu pilgrimage complex on Solophok hill near Namchi with a 108 ft Shiva statue and replicas of the Char Dham and 12 Jyotirlingas.
places.seoDescription: Siddhesvara Dham on Solophok hill, 5 km from Namchi: a 108 ft Shiva statue, models of the Char Dham shrines and replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

images.alt: The 108 ft Shiva statue at Siddhesvara Dham
images.caption: Siddhesvara Dham, Namchi

overview.text:
Siddhesvara Dham, often just called Char Dham, is a Hindu pilgrimage complex on Solophok hill, about 5 km from Namchi. Its centrepiece is a 108 ft seated statue of Shiva that dominates the hilltop and can be seen from much of the surrounding district.

Around it are models of the four Char Dham shrines and replicas of the 12 Jyotirlingas, so pilgrims can visit them all in one place. There is also an 18 ft statue of Kirateshwar. It makes a natural pair with the Guru Padmasambhava statue on Samdruptse, on the hill opposite Namchi.

items.body: See the 108 ft Shiva statue at the top of Solophok hill.
Walk round the models of the Char Dham shrines and the 12 Jyotirlinga replicas.
Pair it with the Guru Padmasambhava statue on Samdruptse, opposite Namchi.

places.name: Tashi View Point
places.summary: Gangtok's classic sunrise viewpoint, facing Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu on clear mornings.
places.seoTitle: Tashi View Point, Gangtok — sunrise over Kanchenjunga
places.seoDescription: Tashi View Point in Gangtok: sunrise views of Kanchenjunga and Siniolchu, open 5 am–6 pm, with tea stalls and nearby Gonjang Monastery.

images.alt: The Tashi View Point platform above Gangtok
images.caption: Tashi View Point, Gangtok

overview.text:
Tashi View Point sits on a hilltop on the edge of Gangtok and is the town's best-known place to watch the sun come up over the Himalayas. On clear days you can see Kanchenjunga and Mount Siniolchu across the valley, with the villages of North Sikkim scattered below.

It opens at 5 am, so come early — the first light on the snow is the reason to be here, and clouds often build later in the day. Tea stalls near the viewpoint sell chai and snacks while you wait. It stays open until 6 pm. Gonjang Monastery, the Himalayan Zoological Park and Bakthang Waterfall are all close by, so it fits easily into a morning round of Gangtok's sights.
